what_its_for: Anagrelide is used to lower the number of platelets (tiny blood cells that help with clotting) in your blood when you have a condition called essential thrombocythemia, which means your body makes too many platelets. Too many platelets can increase your risk of dangerous blood clots or bleeding.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsule.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose, usually 0.5 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day or 1 mg taken twice a day. Your doctor will check your blood counts regularly and slowly adjust your dose until your platelet count reaches a safe level. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store anagrelide at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Store it in a dry place such as a cabinet — not in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking anagrelide, as it may increase your risk of side effects. Avoid taking other medications that can thin your blood, such as aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or blood thinners like warfarin, unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Let your doctor or dentist know you are taking this medicine before any surgery or dental procedure. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain or pounding heartbeat, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, swelling of your legs or ankles, severe headache or dizziness, fainting, unusual or heavy bleeding (such as nosebleeds, bleeding gums, blood in urine or stool), signs of a blood clot (sudden leg pain or swelling, sudden difficulty speaking, vision changes, numbness on one side of the body), stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting that does not go away, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat.
when_it_works: Anagrelide usually begins to lower your platelet count within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment. It may take 4 to 12 weeks to reach your target platelet level. You will need regular blood tests so your doctor can track your platelet counts and adjust your dose if needed. Even if you feel well, continue taking the medication as directed.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Anagrelide may harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Do not breastfeed while taking anagrelide. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially heart-related effects. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver or kidney problems: If you have liver or kidney disease, your doctor may start you on a lower dose and watch you more carefully, as the medication can build up in your body. Children: Safety and dosing for children have not been fully established; your child's doctor will determine the appropriate dose.
